text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers:
- The Slovenian government on Thursday refused to raise wages of railway workers, who threatened to stage a four-hour strike on Tuesday for the second week in a row.
- The parliamentary health board on Thursday decided to approve compensation payment for 15 people who were infected with HIV by blood transfusions in Slovenian hospitals.
- Slovenian Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler on Thursday arrived in Iceland, where he will discuss relations between the two countries and current association processes in Europe.
- A Slovenian foreign ministry delegation on Thursday met Yugoslav counterparts in a bid to try to normalize relations between the two countries.
- The Slovenian ecological fund will offer 1.2 billion tolars ($7.64 million) in loans this year for air pollution prevention projects and building of appropriate infrastructure.
- The ministry of agriculture has so far awarded 200 million tolars in compensation for damage to plants caused by severe weather this winter.

- The ministry of transport said on Thursday it would invest two billion tolars for the reconstruction of 700 km (427 miles) of local roads damaged last winter. The reconstruction is expected to be completed before autumn, the ministry said.
- Ljubljana bourse called on key institutions not to issue any announcements that could influence trading within business hours, in order to ensure fair conditions for all market participants.
